claims.statement: For each fixed independence number a, every ordinary tree T with alpha(T)=a has order at most 2a and hence lies in a finite isomorphism-class search domain; furthermore, all original leaves sharing an original support have identical Delta_p(T-v) selector values and identical selected summands, so their full tagged contribution is exactly their multiplicity times the common summand.
claims.scope: Exact fixed-a finite reduction and same-support compression for finite ordinary trees, preserving the strict selector and tagged aggregate. This provides no uniform bound over a and no sign conclusion for the complete sum.
claims.reason: retained: the bipartition classes are independent, yielding |V(T)|<=2a; at fixed a this bounds a finite isomorphism-class domain. Transposing same-support leaves is an automorphism, preserving T-v, T-{v,s}, and T-N[s] up to the required identity/isomorphism, so strict selector values and summands coincide and multiplicity weighting is exact. This is an elementary fixed-parameter reduction only; it neither runs a census nor bounds compensation across supports, so it gives no universal sign conclusion.

limitations: The finite search bound depends on the unbounded parameter a=alpha(T).
No enumeration was run or claimed; fixed-a finiteness is only a decision reduction.
Compression preserves tagged contributions but supplies no sign control across distinct supports.
The primary lower-region aggregate remains unresolved by this review.
